tldr: EvoSkill v2 (Oct 19) evolves agent skills, meaning instructions, without touching the model or harness. A Oct 26 paper added hierarchical skills for coding agents, and ScienceCUA (Nov 2) built skills from software manuals.
whats_new: EvoGuard (Nov 4) targets degradation when skills evolve online, a failure mode the earlier skill-evolution papers left open.
why_it_matters: Skills are editable text, so agent behavior can change without retraining; online evolution can also make skills worse, so accepted edits need a guard.

beats.headline: EvoSkill v2: a three-agent system that edits skills
Hierarchical skills separate reusable experience from repo-specific context
ScienceCUA builds skills from manuals and evolves them by execution
EvoGuard targets degradation in online skill evolution

open_questions: Do evolved skills hold up on tasks and repositories outside their training benchmark?
Does skill evolution beat hand-written skills on a shared benchmark?
Does EvoGuard's mitigation hold when applied to other evolvers such as EvoSkill v2?
take_for_builders: Version agent skills like code and gate each evolved edit on a grader or benchmark, with a rollback path in case online evolution degrades performance.
